newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Soybean, soymeal prices up in CBOT Project A trade.
newsitem.headline: Soybean, soymeal prices up in CBOT Project A trade.

text.p: Soybean and soymeal prices surged on Friday on the CBOT's Project A trading system in Asia on a bullishly construed weekly crushing report by the U.S. National Oilseed Processors Association (NOPA), traders said on Friday.
The July soybean contract on the Project A after-hours system rose by 15-1/2 U.S. cents to the day's peak of US$8.85 a bushel at 0620 GMT against its close on Thursday of $8.69-1/2.
The July soymeal contract hit a high of $293.00 a ton, up from the previous day's close in Chicago of $288.10 a ton.

A dealer with South Korea's National Livestock Cooperatives Federation said the increase in soybean prices was "due to the bullish weekly crushing report" from the NOPA released after the close of Chicago's open outcry session.
The NOPA said U.S. soybean crushings reached 25,462,000 bushels as of May 28, compared to 22,467,000 bushels in the previous week and 22,792,000 bushels a year ago.

The NLCF trader said the rise in weekly crushing figures raised concerns anew about low U.S. old crop soybean stocks and will probably trigger a fresh rally in the CBOT soy complex when the market opens later on Friday.
